findings.title: Security Advisory - Action Required - July 2026 Security Update
findings.summary_md: Check Point disclosed on July 22, 2026 that CVE-2026-16232, an authentication bypass in SmartConsole login using an application token, had been exploited in the wild against a handful of customers whose Management server was exposed directly to the internet without IP restrictions. The advisory says Smart-1 Cloud customers were already protected and lists fixes in the July 22 jumbo hotfix: R82.10 Take 36, R82 Take 118 and R81.20 Take 158. It also lists six IP addresses observed in exploitation and recommends limiting Trusted Clients and restricting management access with a firewall.

findings.title: Check Point warns of SmartConsole zero-day exploited in attacks
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported on July 23, 2026 that Check Point had patched an actively exploited zero-day, CVE-2026-16232, which lets an unauthenticated attacker obtain an application login token and authenticate to Security Management or Multi-Domain Management as an administrator. Exploitation required an internet-reachable Management server IP and no Trusted Clients restrictions, and Check Point said all affected customers had been notified. The article gives the SmartConsole audit-log check for `Authentication method: application token`, five attacker IPs, and CISA's July 25, 2026 federal remediation deadline.

findings.title: CVE-2026-16232: Critical Check Point SmartConsole Authentication Bypass Exploited in the Wild
findings.summary_md: Rapid7's emergent threat response, first published July 23, 2026, describes CVE-2026-16232 as a CWE-287 authentication bypass rated CVSS 9.1 that yields full administrative privileges on Check Point Management servers. Check Point confirmed in-the-wild exploitation before a patch existed, and CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on July 22 with a July 25 remediation deadline. Rapid7 records fixed builds of R82.10 Take 36, R82 Take 118 and R81.20 Take 158, plus six vendor-published exploit IPs and guidance to hunt administrator, SmartConsole, API and application-token activity.

findings.title: Rapid7 Analysis: Check Point SmartConsole Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-16232)
findings.summary_md: Rapid7 Labs published root-cause analysis and proof-of-concept exploit code for CVE-2026-16232 on July 28, 2026. The bug is a broken trust boundary in which the login service accepts an attacker-supplied SIC distinguished name instead of binding identity to the authenticated peer certificate, then mints an application token and a SmartConsole single sign-on ticket across FWM/CPMI on TCP 18190 and CPM SOAP on TCP 19009. Rapid7 reproduced the exploit on R81.20 and R82.10, confirmed that the vendor hotfixes stop it, and showed that the patched code rejects supplied names that do not match the client certificate DN.

findings.title: PoC Exploit Code Released for Check Point SmartConsole Zero-Day Vulnerability (CVE-2026-16232)
findings.summary_md: eSentire's Threat Response Unit warned on July 29, 2026 that Rapid7 Labs had released proof-of-concept code for CVE-2026-16232 on July 28, lowering the barrier to exploitation of a bug that Check Point had already confirmed was used against a very small number of customers. The advisory explains that the server accepted an attacker-supplied SIC DN without checking it against the authenticated peer certificate, allowing an application token and SmartConsole SSO ticket to be obtained. eSentire assessed with medium confidence that widespread exploitation would follow and urged patching, restricting management access to trusted IPs, and following Check Point hardening guidance.

findings.title: Sept. 16 Advisory: Check Point Quantum Security Management and Log Server Unauthenticated Login Stack Overflow [CVE-2026-91843]
findings.summary_md: Censys published an advisory on September 16, 2026 for CVE-2026-91843, a stack-based buffer overflow in the unauthenticated login of Check Point Quantum Security Management and Log Servers that can execute code as root through an excessively long username. Censys observed 3,836 hosts worldwide presenting the default cp_mgmt SIC identity, while stressing this is total role presence and not a confirmed-vulnerable count. The advisory says Smart-1 Cloud is unaffected, that the flaw was not in CISA KEV or VulnCheck KEV at the time, and that passive scans cannot reveal build or Jumbo Hotfix level.

findings.title: Critical Check Point Management Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code as Root
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported on September 17, 2026 that CVE-2026-91843 is a CVSS 9.8 stack overflow in the pre-authentication login of Check Point Security Management and Log Servers, fixable through LivePatch or Jumbo Hotfix updates. Check Point said there was no indication of exploitation at the time, and Censys reported 3,836 hosts carrying the default management role identity. The article counts CVE-2026-16232, CVE-2026-62144, CVE-2026-18574, CVE-2026-85103 and CVE-2026-91843 as five critical unauthenticated management flaws disclosed since July 22, and notes the July advisory tied CVE-2026-16232 exploitation to management exposed without IP restrictions.
